findings.title: Migration crashes when no `embed_category` row exists in site_settings
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row. `embed_category` defaulted to `''` and only has a DB row if an admin changed it. On most installs the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` raises (IndexError or NoMethodError on nil) and the whole migration aborts. That also blocks the later `category_id == 0` fallback, which was written to handle exactly this case. The same unguarded `[0]['value']` is used for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15. Both lookups need nil-safe handling.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw and unnormalized, via string-interpolated SQL
findings.body: Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated straight into an INSERT: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This skips the model's `before_validation` that strips `http(s)://` and paths. The old setting explicitly allowed values like `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://example.com/1234`, and the old matcher stripped the scheme. Those rows are now stored verbatim, but `record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = <uri.host>`, so they never match. Existing embeds silently stop working after upgrade. The lines are also not stripped of `\r` or whitespace, and a value containing a single quote would break or inject into the SQL. Normalize each host and use `quote`/sanitization.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called with no nil check. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so a request with a missing or empty host key sets `host = nil`. Validation then raises NoMethodError and the client gets a 500 instead of a validation error from `render_json_error`. The in-place `sub!` also mutates the attribute string. Guard with `host.present?`, or assign a new string.

findings.title: Host lookup lowercases the column but not the input, so mixed-case referers are rejected
findings.body: The query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, but `host` is `URI(...).host`, which keeps the case of the referer or embed URL (for example `Blog.Example.com`). The column is lowercased and the parameter is not, so a mixed-case referer never matches and embedding is denied. The host should be downcased before comparing. The format validation accepts uppercase (`/i`), and stored hosts are not downcased on save either.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents two `embeddable_hosts` rows with the same host, either in the model or as a DB unique index. If duplicates carry different categories, `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no ordering. The category chosen for imported topics is then arbitrary. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive) and a unique index.

findings.title: update/destroy dereference nil when the id does not exist
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id (for example a record already deleted in another tab). `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, so both raise NoMethodError and return a 500. Use `find`, or check for nil and respond 404.

findings.title: `update` action and JS `saveChanges` are no-ops
findings.body: `update` just re-serializes the unchanged OpenStruct. The `PUT customize/embedding` route and the controller's `saveChanges` action (`embedding.update({})`) persist nothing, and no template references `saveChanges`. This is dead code that suggests a feature that doesn't exist. Remove the route and action, or implement them.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. Fabrication loads every file, so tests still run. But anyone looking for the category fabricators, or the embeddable_host one, will look in the wrong file. Git history for the category fabricators is lost. The contents should be in the matching files.

findings.title: Admin controller specs only assert inheritance; create/update/destroy are untested
findings.body: Both new admin controller specs only check that the class is a subclass of `AdminController`. Nothing exercises create, update, destroy, the blank-category fallback to uncategorized, validation-error rendering, staff-only access, or the embedding show endpoint. The nil-host and nil-record failure paths above would have been caught by even basic request specs.

findings.title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" test no longer tests what it says
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at embeddable hosts. The test builds a topic with no `has_topic_embed?` stub and `embed_truncate` false by default, so it returns false whatever the hosts are. The test is vacuous and its name is misleading. Either delete it or make it test something real.

findings.title: Plural `_ids` hydration assumes arrays and leaves undefined entries
findings.body: The regex change now matches every `*_ids` key on any REST-serialized payload and calls `obj[k].map(...)` on it. A non-array value there throws and breaks hydration of the whole record. Ids that can't be resolved by `_lookupSubType` yield `undefined` elements in the array. The `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code, because `.map` always returns an array. Templates iterating the collection will then hit undefined items.
